title: The August dip at Calder Quay Hotel
setting: Calder Quay Hotel is a 212-room, eight-floor four-star hotel in the fictional harbour city of Merrowby. A regional management group runs it. An external survey vendor collects its monthly Guest Satisfaction Score (GSS), and the score counts toward the leadership team's bonus. Floors 1-5 hold 128 rooms and floors 6-8 hold 84. Two changes went in this summer: a new self-check-in kiosk system on 23 June, and a new housekeeping contractor from 1 July.
presentingRequest: The Regional VP of Operations wants to know why the August GSS fell from 8.6 to 8.1 and what the hotel should do. She also wants answers on two specific questions: should the hotel give notice to the new housekeeping contractor, and should it pull the self-check-in kiosks?

initialEvidence.source: Email from Dana Okafor-Reyes, Regional VP Operations, to General Manager Tomasz Ellery, 2 September 2026
initialEvidence.text: Tomasz - August GSS came in at 8.1 against our 8.5 target, the first miss in fourteen months. We changed two things this summer: Orrin Facility Group took over housekeeping on 1 July, and the new self-check-in kiosks went live on 23 June. I've read a handful of the August comments and one on a booking site called the room 'tired and dusty'. Complaints logged at the desk are up roughly 40%. My view is that Orrin is the problem and we should serve notice before the 1 October renewal window closes. Please also tell me whether we need to pull the kiosks. I want a recommendation by Friday.

initialEvidence.source: Pellmore Insights GSS dashboard, monthly export for Calder Quay Hotel
initialEvidence.text: Questionnaire version Q7 (in use since January 2025, unchanged). Invitations go to every checked-out stay with a valid email address, as before. July: 412 responses, overall 8.6. August: 398 responses, overall 8.1. By floor block, July to August. Floors 1-5 (128 rooms; 241 August responses): overall 8.6 to 8.5; room comfort 8.4 to 8.3; cleanliness 8.7 to 8.7; check-in 8.8 to 8.8; value for money 8.0 to 7.7. Floors 6-8 (84 rooms; 157 August responses): overall 8.6 to 7.4; room comfort 8.4 to 6.1; cleanliness 8.7 to 8.6; check-in 8.8 to 8.7; value for money 8.0 to 7.3. Vendor note: for this property, month-to-month movements under 0.2 on any score fall within normal variation (trailing 18 months).

04 Aug 15:20 | Chiller CH-2 (east riser, serves floors 6-8) tripped on compressor fault. Reset failed. Guest calls about heat: 23 by 21:00. 05 Aug 09:40 | Contractor diagnosis: failed compressor contactor. Part not in stock; supplier lead time 11 working days. Portable units deployed to 12 rooms (all held). 07-18 Aug | Spot readings in occupied rooms on floors 6-8: 26.5-29.0 C (set point 22). 19 Aug 14:10 | Contactor fitted, CH-2 restored. Floors 6-8 below 23 C by 22:00. Notes: annual preventive maintenance on both CH-2 and CH-1 (west riser, floors 1-5) deferred in April 2026 under a budget hold; neither yet rescheduled. CH-1 has not faulted this year.

initialEvidence.source: Pellmore Insights daily view and verbatim tagging report, August 2026
initialEvidence.text: Floors 6-8 overall score by checkout date: 1-4 Aug 8.5 (n=19); 5-20 Aug 6.8 (n=96); 21-31 Aug 8.4 (n=42); 1-14 Sep 8.6 (n=71). Floors 1-5 daily scores stayed between 8.4 and 8.6 throughout August and early September. Verbatim tagging, August (vendor auto-tags, spot-checked by guest relations): 74 negative comments, 61 of them from floors 6-8. Heat / air conditioning / 'stuffy': 56, all floors 6-8. Cleanliness: 4 (July: 5), 2 per block. Check-in or kiosk: 2 (July: 3). Price or value: 6 (July: 2), 4 of them from floors 1-5. Other: 6.

initialEvidence.source: Rooms division monthly KPI pack, compiled by the Executive Housekeeper and Front Office Manager
initialEvidence.text: Room inspections are done by in-house supervisors, not by the contractor. Pass rate: June 95% (Linthwaite, prior contractor); July 96% (Orrin); August 95% (Orrin), with 95% on floors 1-5 and 95% on floors 6-8. About 640 inspections a month. Front-desk complaint log: July 50 entries, August 71. August by category (July in brackets): room temperature 24 (1); noise 11 (12); housekeeping 9 (10); billing 8 (9); kiosk/check-in 6 (7); other 13 (11). Share of guests checking in at kiosks: July 41%, August 43%. Average queue at peak: July 4.1 min, August 3.9 min. Outage recovery: all 517 floor 6-8 stays checking out 5-20 August received a written apology and a goodwill credit of half a night's rate at checkout.

initialEvidence.source: Note from Priya Vantongeren, Revenue Manager, to the General Manager, 3 September 2026
initialEvidence.text: 'Rack and BAR rates went up 6% hotel-wide from 1 August, as planned in the annual budget. We review rates weekly and can move them at any time. I can't tell you whether that hurt the value score. Value for money dips every August here: last year it went from 8.1 to 7.9 with no rate change, because of festival-season pricing across the city, and the overall score went from 8.5 to 8.4 last August as well. This year's value drop on floors 1-5 is slightly bigger, but nothing I have separates the rate rise from the usual seasonal dip.'

catalogue.title: Orrin Facility Group monthly service reports, July-August 2026
catalogue.text: Monthly service report to Calder Quay Hotel. July / August: rooms serviced 5,812 / 5,990; rooms released by 15:00 98% / 97%; self-audit quality score 97% / 97%; average attendants per shift 21 / 22; two attendant absences in August covered by agency staff. Report note: 'The client notified no service failures in either month. Several attendants reported very warm conditions on floors 6-8 during mid-August and were given extra breaks.'

catalogue.title: Front-office staffing rotas and overtime, June-August 2026
catalogue.text: Front-office rota summary. Headcount: June 18.0 FTE, July 18.5, August 18.0. Overtime hours: June 112, July 96, August 104. In July, two new agents completed kiosk and desk training. No peak-hour shifts went unfilled in July or August. A duty manager was on the rota every night in August.

catalogue.title: Self-check-in kiosk supplier support tickets, June-September 2026
catalogue.text: Support log for Calder Quay. 11 tickets since go-live on 23 June: 8 between 23 June and 6 July (key-card encoder calibration, receipt printer jams), 2 later in July (screen freeze, fixed by restart), 1 in August (receipt paper sensor). Kiosk availability: July 99.1%, August 99.6%. No tickets open at 31 August.

catalogue.title: Public review-site ratings and comments, July-August 2026
catalogue.source: Guest relations extract from public review sites
catalogue.text: July: 58 reviews, average 4.4/5. August: 63 reviews, average 4.1/5. August reviews mentioning heat, air conditioning or stuffy rooms: 19 (July: 0). Mentioning cleanliness or dust: 2 (July: 3). One of these is the 'tired and dusty' review, which also says the room was 'like an oven'. Mentioning check-in: 3 positive, 1 negative. Mentioning price: 3 (July: 2).

catalogue.title: Survey vendor methodology statement, 2026
catalogue.text: Invitations go out 24 hours after checkout to every stay with a valid email address; there is no sampling. Questionnaire version Q7 has been in use since January 2025 with no changes to wording, scale or order. Response rates: June 31%, July 31%, August 30%. The invitation template, timing and reminder schedule have not changed in 2026.

catalogue.title: Building management system corridor temperature trends, August 2026
catalogue.text: Hourly averages from floor 6-8 corridor sensors. 1-3 Aug: 21.8-22.6 C. 4 Aug: rising from 16:00. 6-18 Aug: daytime 27.4-30.2 C, overnight 25.9-27.1 C. 19 Aug: falls from 28.6 C at 14:00 to 22.9 C at 22:00. 20-31 Aug: 21.7-22.8 C. Floor 1-5 corridor sensors stayed at 21.5-23.0 C all through August.

catalogue.title: Guest compensation and room-move ledger, August 2026
catalogue.text: Guest recovery ledger, August. Room moves from floors 6-8 to floors 1-5: 14 (limited by 91% occupancy). Portable cooling units hired: 12, EUR 1,150. Goodwill credits issued at checkout, with a written apology, to all floor 6-8 stays checking out 5-20 August: 517 stays, about EUR 45,750 in total (half of one night's rate each). Credits for all other causes in August: EUR 640 (July: EUR 710).

catalogue.title: Competitive-set guest satisfaction benchmark, June-August 2026
catalogue.source: Merrowby hotel association shared survey programme
catalogue.text: Benchmark across five comparable four-star hotels in Merrowby (anonymised). Average overall guest satisfaction: June 8.4, July 8.4, August 8.3. None of the participating hotels reported a building-systems outage in August. The association does not publish individual hotels' pricing or rate changes.

catalogue.title: Municipal weather station daily records, August 2026
catalogue.text: Daily maximum temperatures: 1-5 Aug 24-27 C; 6-17 Aug 31-35 C (heat advisory 8-16 Aug); 18-31 Aug 23-28 C. The August mean maximum was 29.6 C, against a ten-year August average of 26.1 C.

catalogue.title: Housekeeping staff pulse survey, August 2026
catalogue.source: Anonymous pulse survey of Orrin attendants and in-house supervisors
catalogue.text: 27 responses from 41 invited. 'I have the supplies I need': 85% agree. 'My room quota is manageable': 52% agree (May, under Linthwaite: 49%). 'I am proud of the standard of rooms I hand over': 81% agree. Free-text themes: heat on the upper floors in August (9 mentions), uniform sizing (4), timing of linen deliveries (3).

catalogue.title: Rate change record and occupancy report, July-August 2026
catalogue.text: BAR increase: +6% on all room types from 1 August (budgeted in November 2025). Average daily rate: July EUR 171, August EUR 177 (August 2025: EUR 166). Occupancy: July 88%, August 91% (August 2025: 90%). August channel mix: direct 38%, online agencies 47%, corporate 15% (July: 37 / 48 / 15). The revenue system holds no guest-satisfaction data.

catalogue.title: Finance memo on engineering maintenance deferrals, April 2026
catalogue.source: Director of Finance to General Manager
catalogue.text: Memo, 14 April 2026: 'To meet the Q2 cost target we are moving the following engineering items to Q3: annual preventive service on chillers CH-1 and CH-2 (EUR 6,800 combined, including contactor and relay inspection and the recommended spares kit); cooling-tower descale (EUR 2,100); lobby carpet replacement (EUR 14,000). Engineering notes that the chiller service has been overdue since January. We will revisit this at the July forecast.'

catalogue.title: Food and beverage outlet satisfaction scores, July-August 2026
catalogue.text: Breakfast restaurant: July 8.3, August 8.3. Lobby bar: July 8.1, August 8.2. Room service: July 7.9, August 7.6; August comments mention 'slow' (5) and 'ice delivery' (3). Each outlet gets 90-210 responses a month.

catalogue.title: Loyalty-member complaint emails, August 2026
catalogue.text: 12 complaint emails in August. 9 came from guests on floors 6-8 about room heat between 5 and 18 August; three of them asked why they had not been moved. 1 was about the new rate ('paid more for the same room'). 1 was about late-night noise from a wedding party. 1 was about a duplicated card charge. July had 5 complaint emails, none about temperature.

catalogue.title: Interview with the Chief Engineer, 8 September 2026
catalogue.source: Interview notes, Ruth Abernathy-Sole, Chief Engineer
catalogue.text: 'The contactor is a wear part. The annual service checks it, and the kit we normally buy with the service includes a spare. Without the service we had no spare, so we waited eleven working days for one. CH-1 is the same model and age as CH-2, and its service is overdue too. I can't say CH-1 will fail, but if it does during a hot spell, floors 1-5 go the same way. Apart from that, the units are in reasonable shape.'

hypotheses.text: A failure of in-room cooling during August caused the drop in the overall score.
Problems with check-in after the front-desk system change caused the drop in the overall score.
A decline in housekeeping quality after the contractor change caused the drop in the overall score.
A change in how the guest survey was administered produced the drop in the overall score.
The 1 August room-rate increase contributed to the drop in the overall score.

edges.to: Lower August ratings from guests on floors 6-8

actions.text: Reinstate the deferred preventive maintenance on both chillers, keep critical spare parts on site, and set a written guest-recovery protocol for cooling outages.
Serve notice on the Orrin Facility Group housekeeping contract before the 1 October renewal window.
Reverse the 1 August room-rate increase to restore value-for-money ratings.
Send an apology and a return-stay offer to guests who stayed on floors 6-8 during the cooling outage.
Exclude the August floor 6-8 survey responses from the reported GSS as an outlier month.
